options.text: A square, because all sides are equal and all angles are $90^\circ$, even though the card is tilted.
A rectangle only, because any four-sided shape with right angles is called a rectangle.
A square, because the four sides are equal.
Not a square, because tilting the card changes its side lengths and angles.

stem:
The diagram shows Falguni's four-sided card, tilted on the page. Every side is $6\,\mathrm{cm}$, and every corner is $90^\circ$.

Which claim correctly names the figure?

teacher.key_rationale: All sides equal and all angles 90° make a square; rotation does not change lengths or angles. Calling it only a rectangle, using equal sides alone, or treating tilt as changing measures are wrong.
teacher.figure_note: Tilted square with side labels 6 cm.
